messages:
pagerbot: HIGH PAGER: 3 running jobs in 'dedicated-gpu-pool-2' are hitting repeated NCCL communicator resets. Severity: P1. Auto-escalation to oncall.

devon: got it, I'm oncall. Acknowledge. Which customers? any external-facing SLAs affected?

customer-ops: two customers (cust-alpha, cust-gamma) report job restarts and degraded throughput. Cust-alpha saw 15% request failure for batch infer jobs.

anya: seeing repeated logs on node gnode-07 and gnode-09: `NCCL WARN > Timeout waiting for operation.` followed by `ncclCommInitRank failed: unhandled cuda error` and occasional `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION`.

sam: likely symptom of intermittent PCIe/NVLink drops or driver flaps. Also seeing OOMs on some containers before the reset: `cudaMalloc failed: out of memory` then communicator reset.

mira: copy of the tail logs from one affected pod:```
[2026-03-15T02:04:11Z] NCCL INFO comm 0x7f3b2c8 init rank 2
[2026-03-15T02:04:11Z] NCCL WARN peer 3 timed out waiting for 0x3
[2026-03-15T02:04:11Z] CUDA ERROR 700: an illegal memory access was encountered
[2026-03-15T02:04:12Z] NCCL ERROR: communicators unable to synchronize - aborting
```

devon: thanks. Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) apply temporary placement policy to avoid gnode-07/09, 2) if jobs can tolerate, force single-node fallback for pipeline parallel by setting world_size=1 for scheduling, 3) enable NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 env var for affected jobs.

anya: I'm prepping a node cordon for gnode-07/09. Planning to drain live jobs with `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` and move workloads to spare nodes in the pool. Will annotate nodes with `incident:nccl-peer-reset`.

sam: running a quick health check across the pool:```sh
kubectl get pods -n dedicated --selector=pool=dedicated-gpu-pool-2 -o wide
# look for CrashLoopBackOff or OOMKilled
```
I see 6 pods in CrashLoopBackOff, 4 with OOMKilled.

mira: I'm going to flip NCCL debug to INFO on a canary job to gather more telemetry: add env `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` and `NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0` for one controlled job. Also requesting driver and kernel logs from gnode-07/09: `dmesg | tail -n 200` and `journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced --since "1 hour ago"`

devon: customer impact update: cust-alpha's nightly training job failed 3x and will miss SLA window; cust-gamma's inference latency increased ~35%. Notifying CSMs: @customer-ops please prepare a short blurb.

customer-ops: preparing blurb. ETA 10m.

anya: cordon started w/ maintenance annotation. Draining gnode-07 now. Moves should land on gnode-12 and gnode-14 (spare capacity).

sam: applied a temporary admission controller rule to block new tensor-parallel jobs on the pool for 20m to reduce blast radius. Command:```sh
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: policy/v1beta1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
...
EOF
```

mira: captured NCCL debug from the canary: seeing frequent `ncclGroupEnd` timeouts and inconsistent peer ordering across ranks -> suggests intermittent network packet loss at the NIC or a failing switch.

devon: OK action items for handoff: - anya to continue node drains and validation, - sam to run NIC health checks and collect switch logs, - mira to keep NCCL debug on canary and collect cuda/drivers, - devon will own communications with CSMs until incident triage doc is created.

anya: handing off to night oncall. Will leave playbook updates in the incident thread and tag affected nodes. Next update in 30m unless escalates. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sam: one-off mitigation we validated: setting `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1` on some jobs reduced cross-node collectives and allowed work to progress while we investigate. Not a permanent fix.

mira: note for RCA: correlate NIC counters (rx_errors, drops), switch port flaps, driver upgrade history on gnode-07/09, and recent packing changes to job world_size. Possible root causes: memory fragmentation -> illegal mem access -> communicator abort; or NVLink/PCIe flaps causing asymmetric rank failures.

devon: thanks team. Handoff summary posted to incident doc: https://redwood-internal/incident/1834567890 (draft). If you find evidence of hardware faults, open a hardware ticket with infra-support and tag me.

pagerbot: INCIDENT STATUS: Mitigations applied, ongoing monitoring. Severity remains P1 until customer SLAs are confirmed recovered.

anya: last check: drained nodes show no new NCCL errors on moved pods. Will keep them cordoned until morning.

mira: taking over oncall. Acknowledge handoff.

devon: thanks, handing off.
